title: Walker's Haute Route Finale — Val d'Hérens to Zermatt
subRegion: Valais Alps, Val d'Hérens to Mattertal

bestPeriod.note: The Forcletta and Augstbordpass cols hold snow into early July in a heavy winter; the Europaweg's suspension bridge is closed in high wind, so build a spare day near the end.

summary: The classic final third of the Walker's Haute Route, from Arolla over Val de Moiry and Zinal to Gruben and the Europaweg into Zermatt.
hook: The last stretch of the Walker's Haute Route is where the range earns its reputation: four high cols in five days, each one dropping into a different valley with its own dialect, architecture and cheese. This week starts in Arolla, crosses Val de Moiry to Zinal, climbs to Gruben in the quiet Turtmanntal, and finishes on the Europaweg — the high balcony trail into Zermatt with the Matterhorn filling the skyline for the last two days.

snapshot.Base(s): Arolla to start, Zermatt to finish, huts and village inns between
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 85–95 km, 6,500–7,200 m combined ascent; high alpine col-crossing, white-red-white T3 throughout, one blue-white-blue pitch on the Europaweg approach
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Geneva (GVA), train to Sion, postbus to Les Haudères and on to Arolla
snapshot.Who It Suits: Experienced hut-to-hut hikers with a head for exposure and genuine fitness for consecutive 1,000 m days

itinerary.title: Arolla, acclimatize
itinerary.morning: Train and postbus from Sion via Les Haudères to Arolla (1,998 m), the highest village in Val d'Hérens.
itinerary.afternoon: Short acclimatization walk up toward the Pra Gra viewpoint above the village, checking gear and confirming tomorrow's col conditions with the tourist office.
itinerary.evening: Early dinner; the first col crossing starts tomorrow.
itinerary.dayStats: 6 km, 350 m ascent, 350 m descent. Grade T2, well-graded path, no exposure.

itinerary.title: Col de Riedmatten to Val de Moiry
itinerary.morning: Climb steadily from Arolla to the Col de Riedmatten (2,919 m), a rocky notch with a short chain-assisted step on the northern side, the day's technical crux.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend the long scree slope into Val de Moiry, following the trail down toward the turquoise Lac de Moiry and Cabane de Moiry (2,825 m), a Club Alpin Suisse hut perched above the glacier.
itinerary.evening: The hut terrace faces the Moiry glacier directly; a dramatic first overnight.
itinerary.dayStats: 14 km, 950 m ascent, 550 m descent. Grade T3, chain-assisted rock step at the col, scree descent, no glacier travel required.

itinerary.title: Col de Sorebois into Zinal
itinerary.morning: Descend from Cabane de Moiry along the lake, then climb again to the Col de Sorebois (2,835 m), with wide views over the Val d'Anniviers.
itinerary.afternoon: Long descent into Zinal (1,675 m), a stone-built Anniviers village at the foot of the Weisshorn and Zinalrothorn.
itinerary.evening: Zinal has proper restaurants after two hut nights — worth the extra francs.
itinerary.dayStats: 16 km, 550 m ascent, 1,700 m descent. Grade T3, rocky trail, exposed scree traverse below the col.

itinerary.title: Hotel Weisshorn and the Forcletta
itinerary.morning: Climb out of Zinal on the balcony path to Hotel Weisshorn (2,337 m), a historic mountain hotel dating to 1882, still run as a working refuge with sweeping views over the Weisshorn massif.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue over the Forcletta (2,874 m), the trip's most remote col, descending into the quiet, glacially carved Turtmanntal to reach Gruben.
itinerary.evening: Gruben is one of the smallest overnight stops on the whole Haute Route — book ahead, there are very few beds.
itinerary.dayStats: 19 km, 900 m ascent, 900 m descent. Grade T3, exposed scree on the Forcletta's northern side; can hold snow into early July.

itinerary.title: Augstbordpass to St. Niklaus
itinerary.morning: Climb from Gruben to the Augstbordpass (2,894 m), the last of the week's four high cols, a long steady pull on open alp and scree.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend the extensive switchbacks into the Mattertal at St. Niklaus, the valley's mid-point town on the Zermatt rail line.
itinerary.evening: A valley-floor night, and a chance to dry out gear before the Europaweg.
itinerary.dayStats: 17 km, 850 m ascent, 1,750 m descent. Grade T3, long descent, sustained but not technically difficult.

itinerary.title: The Europaweg to Europahütte
itinerary.morning: Ride the funicular or walk up from St. Niklaus toward the Europaweg, the high balcony trail cut into the Mattertal's western flank, crossing the Charles Kuonen Suspension Bridge — at 494 m, the longest pedestrian suspension bridge in the world when it opened in 2017.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue along the balcony trail, with the Matterhorn now visible up-valley, to Europahütte (2,220 m), a privately run hut used specifically for this crossing.
itinerary.evening: The hut fills with Europaweg walkers exclusively — a sociable last night on the trail.
itinerary.dayStats: 14 km, 950 m ascent, 350 m descent. Grade T3 with one exposed bridge crossing; closed in high wind, so check conditions before committing.

itinerary.title: Into Zermatt
itinerary.morning: The final stretch of the Europaweg continues above Randa and Täsch before dropping to join the valley path into Zermatt, the Matterhorn dead ahead for the whole descent.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive Zermatt (1,608 m), car-free and glacier-ringed; a short walk to the Gornergrat viewpoint train if there is time and energy left.
itinerary.evening: Departure via train to Visp and onward, or an extra night to properly enjoy Zermatt.
itinerary.dayStats: 13 km, 250 m ascent, 900 m descent. Grade T3, forest and balcony path, no further exposure.

accommodationStrategy.name: Cabane de Moiry
accommodationStrategy.description: Booked directly through the SAC/CAS online hut reservation system; the only realistic overnight after the Col de Riedmatten crossing and popular enough in August to need booking weeks ahead.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Weisshorn
accommodationStrategy.description: A privately run refuge-hotel rather than a club hut, with proper rooms as well as dormitory beds; book directly by phone or through its own website, as it does not sit on the SAC reservation system.

accommodationStrategy.name: Europahütte
accommodationStrategy.description: Purpose-built for the Europaweg crossing; book directly through the hut's own reservation page, and confirm bridge-crossing conditions with the warden when you book, since high wind closes it for safety.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European; Switzerland's alpine and helicopter rescue is Rega, reached on **1414** (or 112).
logistics.weather: Valais afternoons build storms quickly above 2,500 m; be over each day's col by midday where possible.
logistics.bookingWindows: Cabane de Moiry and most club huts on this route use the SAC's centralized online reservation portal; book each hut individually as soon as dates are fixed, since August weekends fill three months out.

other.label: Waymarks
other.text: White-red-white paint blazes mark the mountain trail (Bergweg, T2–T3) standard used for most of this route; a small number of blue-white-blue marked sections denote Alpine trail terrain requiring extra care, most notably parts of the Europaweg approach.

other.label: Snow on the cols
other.text: The Forcletta and Augstbordpass are the two most likely to hold snow into early July — ask each hut warden the evening before about conditions on tomorrow's col.

other.label: Currency
other.text: Switzerland uses Swiss francs; carry cash, since several huts and Gruben's small guesthouse have unreliable card connectivity.

other.label: Charles Kuonen bridge
other.text: Closes in high wind for safety; the Europahütte warden and St. Niklaus tourist office both post current status.

proTips: Book Cabane de Moiry, Hotel Weisshorn and Europahütte in that order, immediately after fixing dates — all three are the pinch points of the week.
Ask about Forcletta snow conditions specifically when booking Hotel Weisshorn; the warden tracks it daily in early season.
Carry a printed permit-free itinerary buffer of one extra day near St. Niklaus in case the suspension bridge closes for wind.
Eat the Val d'Anniviers raclette in Zinal rather than waiting for Zermatt — it is a different AOP zone with its own character.
Walk the Europaweg early in the day; afternoon thermal winds off the Mattertal are exactly what closes the bridge.
Use the St. Niklaus funicular to shortcut the first climb onto the Europaweg if Day 6's legs are tired from the Augstbordpass descent.
Reserve a Gornergrat train slot for Day 7 afternoon if the week has gone to schedule — it sells out on clear days.

packingNotes: Trekking poles, essential for the long scree descents off Sorebois and the Augstbordpass.
A warm layer for col crossings above 2,800 m even in August.
Hüttenschlafsack for every hut night on the route.
Gaiters if early-season snow is reported on the Forcletta or Bockkarscharte-style shaded gullies.
A head for the Charles Kuonen bridge — it is engineered and safe, but genuinely exposed and moves underfoot.
2 L water capacity; cols are dry, valleys are not.
Cash in Swiss francs for huts and Gruben.
Sun protection rated for high altitude; UV is intense on the open col traverses.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Snow blocks the Forcletta or Augstbordpass.** Fallback: descend to the valley floor and use the Sierre–St. Niklaus postbus/rail link to bypass the col, rejoining the route at the next hut.

**Charles Kuonen bridge closed for wind.** Fallback: the St. Niklaus valley path to Randa and on to Zermatt is a genuine, well-marked lower alternative that misses the bridge but keeps the week intact.
**Cabane de Moiry fully booked.** Fallback: descend from the Col de Riedmatten directly to Grimentz instead, staying in the village and rejoining the route at Zinal the next day.

**Weather locks in for 48 hours.** Fallback: Zinal and St. Niklaus both have onward rail or postbus links, letting you skip a col day entirely and rejoin further along rather than losing the whole week.

**Fatigue after four consecutive col days.** Fallback: the itinerary is honestly demanding; splitting Day 4 into two shorter days by overnighting at Hotel Weisshorn only and detouring to Gruben the next morning is a legitimate adjustment.
